gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 24?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 24 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from sources including GFS and ECMWF indicate a stable high-pressure regime with easterly flow and partly cloudy skies over Munich on August 24, supporting afternoon highs near the long-term average of 23.4 °C. Recent observations show overnight lows around 11–13 °C rising gradually under light winds, with minimal cloud cover limiting further warming or cooling. This consensus positions 24 °C (market-implied 56.5 %) and 23 °C (31.5 %) as the dominant outcomes, reflecting typical late-summer variability of roughly ±1 °C around the mean. No incoming fronts or significant moisture advection are expected to alter the trajectory before resolution, though minor model spread in boundary-layer mixing accounts for the residual probability on adjacent values.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction ensembles from the ECMWF and German Weather Service (DWD) point to a maximum temperature in Munich on August 25 most likely between 21–23 °C, aligning with the market’s tight clustering around those outcomes and the 38 % implied probability for 23 °C or higher. Cooler-than-average conditions observed across central Europe earlier in the week have tempered expectations for stronger warming, while upcoming high-resolution model runs and observational updates from surface stations will further refine the temperature distribution before resolution.

Traders have concentrated probability on 32–33°C because ensemble spreads and short-term model runs show limited upside beyond 34°C and little downside risk below 31°C, consistent with the observed stability in steering patterns and minimal change in guidance over the past 24 hours. 

Upcoming JMA updates and any afternoon convection will be the key near-term drivers before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Mild late-summer conditions and stable forecast models position 21–22 °C as the dominant outcomes for London’s highest temperature on August 24.** Official guidance from the Met Office and BBC Weather shows a daytime maximum near 23 °C under partly cloudy skies with light easterly winds and negligible precipitation risk, aligning with the market’s heavy weighting toward 22 °C (50.5 %) and 21 °C (38.5 %). These values sit close to the long-term August average high of roughly 21–22 °C at central London stations. 

Recent model runs have shown little day-to-day shift, with no incoming Atlantic fronts or strong southerly flow to boost temperatures toward 24 °C or higher. The low probabilities assigned to 23 °C (8.0 %) and above reflect both the modest forecast ceiling and the narrow margin required for an official reading to reach those thresholds. Traders are therefore pricing the outcome primarily on the consensus maximum from verified observing sites rather than any rapidly evolving atmospheric drivers.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency point to a daily maximum of 34–35°C in Tokyo on August 25 amid a strong Pacific high-pressure system maintaining above-normal late-summer temperatures.** Southerly winds are advecting warm, humid maritime air with dew points near 25°C, while mostly sunny conditions and light afternoon cloud development are expected to allow strong solar heating. Ensemble model guidance shows a narrow range centered on 33–35°C, with slight downside risk if scattered convection develops earlier than anticipated and caps the peak. Historical August extremes in Tokyo rarely exceed 36°C without typhoon influence, supporting the market’s tight clustering around 33°C and 34°C as the most probable outcomes under current steering patterns. Updated JMA guidance and regional model runs over the next 12–18 hours will be the key catalysts for any shift in trader consensus.

Official Met Office guidance points to a maximum of 22–23°C across London and the southeast, driven by sunny spells after early fog clearance, an easterly breeze, and daytime heating under high pressure. Historical August maxima for London average near 21–22°C, providing a climatological anchor that reinforces the current market focus.

Because resolution depends on the single official daily maximum (typically recorded at a standardized site like Heathrow), even small deviations in observed peak—arising from micro-scale variations in cloud or wind—can shift the outcome between the two leading brackets. eventMetadata.context_description: Recent short-range ensemble forecasts from the GFS and European models, converging on daytime highs of 26–28 °C for Munich on August 26 under partly to mostly cloudy skies with light winds and a low risk of early showers, form the main driver behind the market’s clustering around these outcomes. Recent model runs show narrow spread after a period of stable, near-normal conditions across southern Germany, reducing the likelihood of outliers above 29 °C or below 25 °C. Traders therefore price the highest implied probabilities on 27 °C and 28 °C, consistent with official guidance from agencies such as the German Weather Service and observed trends in late-summer temperature variability. Updated model guidance expected within the next 24 hours could refine these probabilities as the event nears resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and official guidance converge on a daytime high of 21–22 °C for Munich on August 25, 2026, under mostly cloudy skies with showers or thunderstorms expected.** Multiple sources, including GFS-derived outlooks, WeatherBug, Weather Atlas, and regional German services, indicate a high near 21–22 °C (roughly 70–72 °F), with lows around 14–15 °C overnight. This is slightly below the long-term August average high of about 23 °C.

The primary scientific drivers are increased cloud cover and precipitation tied to a westerly or northwesterly flow advecting cooler, moister Atlantic air. Rain probabilities reach 55–69 % during the day, which reduces incoming solar radiation and promotes evaporative cooling. Light to moderate winds (5–7 mph or 8–11 km/h) further limit boundary-layer mixing and daytime warming. Recent observations on August 24 showed partly cloudy conditions with highs around 22–24 °C, setting up a transition to more unsettled weather.

Market-implied probabilities—led by 23 °C or higher at 38 %, followed closely by 21 °C (23 %) and 22 °C (22.5 %)—reflect model consensus around these values while incorporating uncertainty from timing of showers, exact cloud breaks, and any urban heat-island effects at the Munich Airport station used for resolution. Traders appear to weigh the risk of brief clearing allowing a brief spike above 22 °C against the cooling influence of expected precipitation. Upcoming short-range model updates and radar trends through the morning of the 25th will likely refine these odds as the day progresses.

Trader consensus across the closely matched 25–27°C outcomes reflects this narrow forecast spread and typical model divergence on exact timing of frontal passages two days ahead, alongside London's urban heat-island effect that can add 1–2°C locally at official stations. Updated short-range guidance expected from the Met Office will likely refine these probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Building high pressure and sunny conditions under a ridge are steering NYC toward a daytime maximum in the low 80s on August 24, 2026.** National Weather Service forecasts and model consensus project a high near 80–82 °F, with mostly sunny skies, light southwest winds, and minimal cloud cover or moisture limiting further warming or cooling. This setup aligns with late-summer climatology for the region, where subsidence beneath the ridge suppresses convection and supports efficient daytime heating without extreme heat advection. 

Trader-implied probabilities heavily favor the 80–81 °F (60.5 %) and 82–83 °F (31.5 %) bins because official guidance and ensemble runs show tight clustering around these values, with little spread toward higher or lower thresholds. Minor uncertainties remain around exact wind speeds and boundary-layer mixing, but no significant model disagreement or incoming frontal systems appear likely to shift the outcome outside the low-to-mid 80s before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and model guidance indicate a high near 78–80°F for New York City on August 25, driven by modest northwesterly flow behind a weak front that limits afternoon mixing and caps temperatures slightly below late-August climatology (average highs ~82–83°F). eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts project a clear to partly cloudy day over Tokyo on August 25 with a maximum of 35°C, driven by a strong Pacific High advecting warm air masses. Traders have priced 33–34°C as the modal outcomes, reflecting ensemble model spread, potential for modest afternoon cooling from boundary-layer mixing, and historical verification biases in urban stations where the heat island effect adds 1–2°C above rural baselines. Late-summer climatology shows typical daily maxima of 31–35°C, with low precipitation chances limiting further modulation. The tight clustering around these values underscores genuine forecast uncertainty ahead of final observational data release.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 24 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance and ensemble forecasts for August 25 indicate a settled easterly flow under high pressure, with sunny intervals and light winds supporting a daytime maximum of 23–25 °C across London. The tight clustering of market-implied probabilities around these values reflects residual uncertainty in afternoon cloud cover and boundary-layer mixing, which can alter peak readings by 1–2 °C depending on whether scattered fair-weather cumulus thickens or clears. Warmer 26 °C outcomes remain less likely absent stronger continental advection, while cooler results would require earlier or more extensive cloud. Updated high-resolution model runs and the next Met Office briefing this evening will further refine surface temperature expectations before resolution.

Historical late-August climatology places Tokyo's average daily maximum near 31°C, providing context for the current elevated trader-implied odds around 34–35°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast consensus from DWD, ECMWF, and GFS models positions 24°C as the most likely daily maximum for Munich on August 24, 2026.** Stable high pressure with moderate northeasterly flow and partly cloudy skies limits daytime heating, producing afternoon highs near the long-term average of 23.4°C while keeping conditions dry. Midday observations around 21–22°C align with model guidance showing limited further rise, consistent with the market’s 80.5% implied probability for 24°C. Minor model spread supports the smaller probabilities assigned to 23°C and 25°C, with negligible odds for extremes given the current synoptic pattern and absence of significant warm-air advection or clearing that would push temperatures higher.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest ensemble guidance from the Met Office and ECMWF has tightened around a daily maximum near 23–24 °C for London on 25 August, driving the near-even market split between those two outcomes. Persistent high pressure supports mostly sunny intervals and light winds, limiting rapid daytime heating, while modest low-level moisture and a slight chance of afternoon cloud or isolated showers introduce small downward bias to the peak reading at official stations such as London City Airport. Historical August climatology places typical maxima around 22 °C, so current model consensus sits slightly above average yet short of the warmer scenarios that would push readings to 25 °C or higher. Traders are watching the next model runs and 24-hour observational updates for any shift in boundary-layer conditions that could alter the exact recorded high by a degree.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts and ensemble model consensus point to a daytime high of 33–35 °C for Tokyo on 26 August 2026, with the market’s tight clustering between 34 °C (36.5 %) and 35 °C (29.5 %) reflecting this narrow range.** 

Persistent summer high pressure and above-average sea-surface temperatures in the western Pacific have sustained elevated baseline warmth, while the urban heat-island effect in central Tokyo can add 1–2 °C above rural stations. Afternoon cloud build-up and a modest chance of late showers—already signaled in several guidance runs—could cap the peak near 33–34 °C if convection develops earlier than expected; conversely, clearer skies or delayed precipitation would favor 35 °C or slightly higher. Historical late-August maxima average ~31–32 °C, so the current setup represents modest positive anomaly. Traders are therefore focused on the next 48-hour model updates from JMA and global ensembles, particularly any shift in timing of the rain threat or adjustments to boundary-layer mixing, which will determine whether the highest reading settles at the lower or upper end of the favored 33–35 °C window.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts and ensemble model consensus point to a daytime high of 33–35 °C for Tokyo on 26 August 2026, with the market’s tight clustering between 34 °C (36.5 %) and 35 °C (29.5 %) reflecting this narrow range.** 

Persistent summer high pressure and above-average sea-surface temperatures in the western Pacific have sustained elevated baseline warmth, while the urban heat-island effect in central Tokyo can add 1–2 °C above rural stations. Afternoon cloud build-up and a modest chance of late showers—already signaled in several guidance runs—could cap the peak near 33–34 °C if convection develops earlier than expected; conversely, clearer skies or delayed precipitation would favor 35 °C or slightly higher. Historical late-August maxima average ~31–32 °C, so the current setup represents modest positive anomaly. Traders are therefore focused on the next 48-hour model updates from JMA and global ensembles, particularly any shift in timing of the rain threat or adjustments to boundary-layer mixing, which will determine whether the highest reading settles at the lower or upper end of the favored 33–35 °C window.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 25 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 25 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 25 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts from major meteorological sources position Munich’s August 25 daytime maximum near 22–24 °C under partly cloudy to overcast skies with light westerly winds and possible early sprinkles.** These conditions reflect typical late-August climatology in southern Germany, where average highs decline from mid-month peaks near 25 °C toward 21–23 °C as solar insolation decreases and Atlantic air masses exert greater influence. Ensemble guidance, including recent GFS runs, shows modest warming under broken cloud cover but limited instability or clear-sky heating that would push readings into the mid-20s or higher.

The market’s heaviest weighting on 23 °C or above (40 %), followed by 21 °C (25.5 %) and 22 °C (18.5 %), aligns with this consensus range while incorporating the small but non-zero chance that clearer breaks or slightly stronger southerly flow could add 1–2 °C. Lower-probability outcomes below 20 °C would require persistent thick cloud cover or heavier rain not currently indicated by operational models. Updated National Meteorological Service and private-model runs expected overnight or early on the 25th remain the key near-term catalysts that could shift implied probabilities before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 25 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Model consensus remains tight with limited spread, though minor cloud increases or localized sea-breeze effects could trim the peak by 1°C. Traders appear to weigh these stable thermal and circulation factors heavily, with implied probabilities concentrated in the narrow 33–35°C window ahead of final observational confirmation.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency project a 33°C high for Tokyo on August 26 under cloudy conditions with scattered showers possible, while some models allow modest upside to 34–35°C if daytime heating strengthens beneath lingering summer high pressure. Trader consensus clustering around 34°C and 35°C reflects uncertainty in cloud cover, precipitation timing, and localized urban heat-island effects that can add 1–2°C above regional baselines. Above-normal seasonal temperatures driven by an expanded Pacific High continue to support elevated readings, yet increasing moisture and potential afternoon convection introduce downside risk that differentiates the tightly matched 33–35°C outcomes. Updated JMA guidance and ensemble model runs expected in the next 24–48 hours will likely refine these probabilities ahead of market resolution.
